candidates.evidence: The only strong line is at 181.4 cm-1 (FWHM about 8 cm-1). A weak, broad feature sits near 140 cm-1. The strong line is the closest match to the A1g(2) mode, and the 140 cm-1 feature is the closest match to Eg(2). Both lie 7-9 cm-1 above the usual positions (about 174 and 131 cm-1), and A1g(1) near 72 cm-1 is not seen. Only the 532 nm laser, a Raman spectrum and a layered-material context support this identification.
Its main modes are Eg(2) near 103, A1g(2) near 134 and A1g(1) near 62 cm-1. None of these match a dominant line at 181 cm-1.
It has its strongest lines near 190 and 210 cm-1 and a broad band around 150-160 cm-1. The single sharp line at 181 with no companion near 210 does not fit.
Its modes are near 69, 112 and 165 cm-1, so the 181 cm-1 line is 16 cm-1 too high.

hint_reasoning: No material hint was given in the metadata, so the identification rests on the spectrum alone.

peaks.assignment: A1g(2) out-of-plane Bi-Se stretch (blue-shifted vs. the usual ~174 cm-1)
peaks.source: Gaussian fit of the 60-260 cm-1 window gives position 181.40 ± 0.1 and FWHM 7.8 ± 0.3 cm-1. Assignment by comparison with Richter et al., Phys. Status Solidi B 84, 619 (1977), and Zhang et al., Nano Lett. 11, 2407 (2011), where bulk A1g(2) is about 174 cm-1.

peaks.assignment: Eg(2) in-plane mode (tentative, weak and broad)
peaks.source: The fitted hump is at about 140 ± 1 cm-1, with an amplitude of about 950 counts against noise of about 370. It is only about 2.5 sigma, so its assignment is tentative. Compared with Eg(2) near 131 cm-1 in Richter 1977.

peaks.assignment: A1g(1) expected here but not detected
peaks.source: Richter et al. 1977 give A1g(1) near 72 cm-1. The measured counts at 60-85 cm-1 average 6095, against 6122 at 90-110 cm-1, so there is no peak.

properties.name: layered chalcogenide structure
properties.value: Consistent with a rhombohedral (D3d^5) Bi2Se3-type quintuple-layer crystal
properties.source: Based on the match to the A1g(2) and Eg(2) positions

properties.name: blue shift of modes vs. bulk
properties.value: About +7 cm-1 on A1g(2). The cause cannot be determined. Possibilities include compressive strain, a different composition or a different crystal phase.

properties.name: background
properties.value: Sloping, fluorescence-like baseline. The signal-to-noise ratio is low, and the noise is about 370 counts on a baseline of 5000-7000 counts.

citations: Richter, Becker, Renker, Phys. Status Solidi B 84, 619 (1977)
limits: The identification rests on one strong line plus one weak, broad feature. It is a best match and not a unique fingerprint.

The 181 cm-1 line is about 7 cm-1 above the usual Bi2Se3 A1g(2) position. The Eg(2) hump is about 9 cm-1 high. I cannot say whether this comes from strain, a different composition, calibration offset or another material.
A1g(1) near 72 cm-1 is absent. This could be because the signal-to-noise ratio is low or because of the sample, and I cannot tell which.
The data are not angle-resolved, so the polarization pattern of each mode is unknown. The irreps are assigned only by position.
The noise is high, so weak features such as the 140 cm-1 hump and any broad features above 250 cm-1 cannot be assigned. Peaks found in the noise above 250 cm-1 were not treated as real.
No Si peak at 520.7 cm-1 is detectable. The substrate is not given in the metadata, and it cannot be identified from these data.
Layer number, doping and strain cannot be quantified from a single unpolarized spectrum.
